subjects.name: Slave patrols in the American South

summary: The first Behind the Police episode traces how American policing grew out of colonial night watches and, in the South, out of the slave patrols that hunted, whipped and set dogs on enslaved people, a lineage running to police dog attacks in Ferguson.

evidence.note: colonial night watches begin with Boston in 1636, the earliest period treated as part of the story
Peel's 1829 London Metropolitan Police as the first modern force, model for Boston in 1838
first slave patrol created in the Carolina colony in 1704
zoom in on Missouri: slave patrols from statehood, lash quotas by 1845
patrol bloodhounds turned on Union troops; Black regiments fight them in 1862 and 1864
after 1865 Southern slave patrols turn into formal police departments
DOJ report after Michael Brown's 2014 killing finds Ferguson police dogs bit only Black people

notes: Primary subject is the slave patrol as an institution, so no roles. Sparta's Crypteia, Athens, Rome and the English frank pledge (about 11 minutes) are pre-story background and comparison, so covered_span starts with the 1636 colonial watch; Crypteia kept as a keyword. Ferguson 2014-2015 is a real segment; the 2020 uprising framing sets reaches_present. GB is for the Peel segment only.
